sheets.name: README
rows: Keep this workbook together with Vipin_Gym_Codex_Context_2026-08-07.md.
Before workout: record sleep, energy, soreness/pain, weakness, and movement restriction.
During workout: record every set, weight basis, reps, form/assistance, Set Type, and RIR.
After workout: update Session Summary, Exercise Targets, recovery, and coaching notes.
Weekly: review average morning weight, Sunday waist, steps/cardio, protein adherence, and performance.
Every ~4 weeks: add standardized front, side, and back progress-photo references.
Never silently replace uncertain numbers; mark them To verify or Not recorded.
The Dashboard is driven by Session Summary; do not manually type KPI totals.
Nutrition targets remain provisional until health, diet pattern, schedule, and intake are verified.
Create dated backups periodically; local files are the durable source of truth.
New sheets: Session Summary, Coaching Profile, Nutrition Plan, Photos & Measurements, Protein Calculator.

markdownSections.title: Progression rules
markdownSections.raw:
- Main lifts: mostly 8–10 or 8–12 reps.
- Isolation: mostly 10–15 reps.
- Increase reps before load.
- Assisted reps are not equivalent to clean reps.
- Record whether weight is total, plates each side, or each dumbbell.
- Core rule: **earn the next weight before increasing it.**

markdownSections.title: Session logging protocol
markdownSections.raw:
Before each workout record:

- Sleep hours and quality.
- Energy from 1–5.
- Relevant soreness from 0–10.
- Any pain: location, severity, and whether muscular or joint-based.
- Weakness or restricted movement.

For every exercise record:

- Weight and whether it is total, each side, or each dumbbell.
- Repetitions.
- Set Type: Warm-up, Working, Back-off, Drop, or Assisted.
- Estimated RIR for working sets.
- Form, assistance, and pain notes.

After each workout update the Workout Journal, Session Summary, Exercise Targets, Recovery & Body sheet, this Markdown history, coaching assessment, and next-session targets.

markdownSections.title: Weekly review protocol
markdownSections.raw:
- Record morning body weight on at least three days when practical; use the weekly average rather than one reading.
- Record waist at the navel on Sunday morning after the bathroom and before food.
- Review protein adherence, steps/cardio, sleep, soreness, workout performance, and waist trend together.
- Do not change calories or training volume from a single unusual weigh-in or workout.

markdownSections.title: Sleep and caffeine coaching assessment
markdownSections.raw:
- Coffee is taken before a roughly 21:00 workout, about five hours before the usual 02:00 bedtime. Late caffeine is a plausible contributor to the sleep challenge.
- The exact EAA+ product must be verified. The currently listed MuscleTech Platinum 100% EAA+ product page does not identify caffeine, but that does not prove Vipin's specific product or version is caffeine-free.
- Initial experiment: for 7–14 days, use decaf or no late pre-workout coffee and ensure the intra-workout product is caffeine-free, then record sleep onset, awakenings, morning freshness, and gym energy. Change one variable at a time.
- Research context: a controlled trial found 400 mg caffeine disrupted sleep even six hours before bedtime, and a later meta-analysis found caffeine reduced sleep time and sleep efficiency. Individual dose and sensitivity vary.

References used for the coaching assessment:

- FDA caffeine overview: https://www.fda.gov/consumers/consumer-updates/spilling-beans-how-much-caffeine-too-much
- MuscleTech Platinum 100% EAA+ product page: https://www.muscletech.com/products/platinum-100-eaa
- Drake et al. caffeine/sleep trial: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24235903/
- Gardiner et al. systematic review and meta-analysis: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36870101/

markdownSections.title: Revised late-workout caffeine decision
markdownSections.raw:
- A full serving of EAA+ Energy already supplies 100 mg caffeine. The half-spoon black coffee adds an unknown amount, so the combined dose is more than 100 mg but cannot be calculated yet.
- Immediate coaching target: **do not combine the black coffee with this EAA+ Energy product** during the approximately 21:00 workout.
- First controlled test: use no pre-workout coffee for 7 nights, record the actual EAA+ scoop and finishing time, and track sleep onset, awakenings, morning freshness, and workout energy.
- If sleep remains difficult, replace EAA+ Energy with a caffeine-free EAA/electrolyte drink or water for the next 7 nights while keeping the rest of the routine stable.
- The EAA+ product alone is not proven to be the cause of the sleep problem. A 2025 randomized crossover trial in 23 moderately caffeinated young men found no significant objective or subjective sleep effect from 100 mg caffeine taken four hours before bedtime, while 400 mg showed clear disruption. Individual sensitivity and the additional coffee dose still matter.

Additional research reference:

- Gardiner et al., dose and timing effects of caffeine on subsequent sleep: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39377163/

markdownSections.title: Why a 39-inch navel waist can coexist with size-34 trousers
markdownSections.raw:
- Trouser waistbands commonly sit below the navel, where the torso circumference may differ.
- The labelled trouser size is not guaranteed to equal the garment’s physical circumference.
- Brand cut, stretch fabric and vanity sizing can make a labelled size smaller than the actual garment measurement.
- Body-composition tracking uses a consistent anatomical measurement, not the clothing label.

For future waist checks: use a bare abdomen; stand relaxed; keep the tape horizontal through the navel; take the reading after a normal exhale without sucking in the stomach; keep the tape snug without compressing the skin. Take two readings and repeat if they differ by more than 0.5 cm. The next comparable Sunday reading should use the same conditions and location.

markdownSections.title: Coaching assessment
markdownSections.raw:
The session produced valuable progression on chest-supported row and especially the iso-lateral high row. It remained free of joint pain and assisted repetitions, and sleep quality afterward was Good.

However, the statement that every target was met is not supported by the actual log. Lat pulldown did not reach the planned 55 kg x 11; seated cable row fell from the previous 60 kg x 9 to 60 kg x 8; straight-arm pulldown did not reach 50 kg x 13-15; and the hyperextension target was exceeded in load while missing the prescribed reserve. The session contained **20 working-level sets**: one at RIR 3, fifteen at RIR 2, three at RIR 1 and one at RIR 0. Final energy fell from Medium-High to Low, and lower-back pump developed after the unplanned +20 kg hyperextension.

The central issue remains volume and effort distribution, not lack of strength. First sets at RIR 2 are stimulating working sets, even when informally treated as warm-ups. The next Back session must use genuine low-fatigue preparation sets, exactly 15 working sets and no RIR 0 work.
